sentences.t: 2010: Nithin and Nikhil Kamath found Zerodha in Bengaluru as a discount brokerage.
The name joins "zero" with "rodha", Sanskrit for barrier.
Six employees, ₹2 crore from Nithin's savings and a Singapore-based friend (Wikipedia).
2010 onwards: flat ₹20 per executed order on intraday and F&O trades; equity delivery commission-free (Wikipedia).
2013: Kailash Nadh joins to start the technology team and stays CTO; the platforms are built in-house (Wikipedia).
2014: Rainmatter, an early-stage fintech fund, is set up; it later backs CRED, Smallcase, Sensibull, GoldenPi and WintWealth (Wikipedia).
2019: Zerodha overtakes ICICI Securities as India's largest retail broker by active clients.
True Beacon, an alternative investment fund, starts the same year (Wikipedia).
2020: a self-assessed $1 billion valuation through an ESOP buyback.
Customers grow from about 1.3 million in early 2020 to nearly 10 million by the end of 2022 (Wikipedia).
2023: Zerodha Fund House launches with Smallcase, selling direct-only index funds that pay no distributor commissions (Wikipedia).
2025-26: invests in market-data platform Tijori Finance (Nov 2025) and gets a merchant banking licence through Zerodha Corporate Advisors (2026), per Wikipedia.
Zerodha spent ₹47 crore on advertising in FY25, about 0.5% of its ₹8,847 crore revenue (our calculation from the Entrackr figures).

Its distribution runs on free education and word of mouth: Varsity, Daily Brief, Zero1 and other content properties that Kamath says have become default places to learn finance, and Varsity Live, which crossed 2 lakh registrations for a free course (Z-Connect).
Kamath also describes a deliberate stance against growth tricks: no trackers or analytics in the apps, no revenue-driven A/B testing, no notifications engineered to make people trade.
He frames this as philosophy; functionally, it means acquisition cost stays near zero while competitors pay for installs.
A Mint article cited in the same post notes Zerodha is the only broker that does not ask for intrusive app permissions.
Account opening was made free in February 2024, and equity delivery trades carry no brokerage (Z-Connect, Wikipedia).
The pricing removes every reason not to start.
The paid product is the active trader: ₹20 per executed intraday or F&O order.
Kamath's own framing is blunt about where revenue comes from: "almost every brokerage business model relies on earnings from active traders who trade options" (Z-Connect).

FY25 revenue of ₹8,847 crore across 7.26 million users works out to roughly ₹12,200 per user per year (our calculation; the user count is NSE data cited by Entrackr and is not the same base as paying traders, so treat this as an average, not per-trader yield).
Brokerage is the primary stream; interest income, software services and investment-management fees add to it (Entrackr).

The cost base is small for the scale: total FY25 costs were ₹3,238 crore, including ₹539 crore of salaries and ₹2,328 crore of fees and commissions, producing a 63.78% EBITDA margin and 32% ROCE (Entrackr).
The repeat business is not a subscription; it is that client money stays on the platform.
Assets held by Zerodha customers account for about 10% of all retail and HNI assets in the country (Z-Connect).

On top of that base, newer products compound: the Margin Trading Facility, which lets clients buy shares with borrowed money, reached a book of about ₹5,000 crore and roughly 5% market share within nine months of launch, and Zerodha Capital's loan-against-securities book stands at ₹430 crore with same-day disbursal (Z-Connect).

Zerodha's exchange-calculated net worth is a little over ₹13,000 crore (LC Gupta method, which excludes private investments and discounts pledged assets), more than 50% of the client funds it handles on any given day, with zero debt (Z-Connect).
FY25 cash and bank balances were ₹22,679 crore against total current assets of ₹35,719 crore (Entrackr).

It self-hosts core systems, so customer data stays on its own infrastructure, publishes incident disclosures without being required to, and runs Kite Backup, a WhatsApp-based emergency trading channel on separate infrastructure (Z-Connect).
Kamath presents the no-dark-patterns stance as a trust moat; the financial cushion is what lets him keep it when revenue falls.
FY25 was the first down year in the company's public record.

Revenue from operations fell 11.5% to ₹8,847 crore from ₹9,993 crore, and net profit fell 22.9% to ₹4,237 crore from ₹5,496 crore (RoC statements via Entrackr; a Tracxn-based report by Indian Startup News puts revenue at ₹8,868.2 crore and profit at ₹4,236.7 crore, a small difference in source data, shown here as reported by each).
The company still paid ₹1,395 crore in taxes, and directors Nithin Kamath, Nikhil Kamath and Seema Patil drew ₹228 crore in combined remuneration (Entrackr).
The cause is regulatory, and Kamath names it himself.

SEBI's steps to cool retail F&O speculation - a higher securities transaction tax on options, fewer weekly expiries, a higher basic-services demat limit, and removal of the exchange transaction-charge rebate - began biting from October 2024.

In the June 2025 quarter, brokerage revenue fell about 40% from a year earlier, and Kamath wrote that regulators are evaluating whether to stop weekly options altogether, in which case Zerodha would be "forced to start charging brokerage for equity delivery trades" to keep the business tenable (Z-Connect).

Active clients fell from 7.95 million in February to 7 million in October 2025 on NSE data, while Groww, which listed in November 2025, holds 12 million active users; Groww's September-quarter profit rose 12% to ₹471.33 crore even as its revenue fell 9.5% (Indian Startup News).

The risk, in one lineZerodha's moat is its balance sheet and trust; its exposure is that the revenue engine sits on a product, retail options trading, that the regulator considers harmful and is actively shrinking.
The FY25 decline is small because the rules landed mid-year; the June 2025 quarter's 40% brokerage fall is the fuller picture, in the founder's own numbers.
Distribution can be a by-product of generosity.
Free education and zero-friction pricing replaced a marketing budget; advertising was about 0.5% of revenue in FY25 (Entrackr figures, our calculation).
Let the customer keep the first product free and charge where intensity is highest.
Delivery investing is free; the ₹20 fee sits on frequent F&O and intraday orders (Wikipedia).
The risk is that regulators can see the same concentration.
A balance sheet is a strategy, not an outcome.
Net worth above 50% of client funds and zero debt (Z-Connect) are what allow Zerodha to refuse dark patterns and survive a 40% quarterly brokerage fall without changing its model.
Founder pessimism is cheap insurance.
Kamath publicly expected the regulatory hit years before it came, and judges the business on a five-year moving average rather than quarterly growth (Z-Connect).
The trade-off is visible too: Groww now has nearly twice the active clients (Indian Startup News).
Adjacencies spread the bet slowly.

Asset management, loans against securities, MTF, merchant banking and the Rainmatter portfolio each reduce reliance on options income, but none is yet large enough to replace it (Wikipedia, Z-Connect).
